articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Piura alcanza los 25 °C durante la noche y establece un nuevo récord histórico en octubre
articles.summary: Piura alcanzó los 25 °C durante la noche del 30 de octubre y estableció un nuevo récord de temperatura nocturna para este mes.
articles.body_text: Piura registró este viernes 30 de octubre una temperatura nocturna de 25.0 °C, estableciendo un nuevo récord histórico para este mes. El registro representa la noche más cálida de octubre desde que se tienen mediciones y refleja las condiciones de calor que afectan a esta región del norte del país. De acuerdo con la información difundida por la Asociación de Astronomía y Meteorología (ASSIMET), con datos de la Corporación Peruana de Aeropuertos y Aviación Comercial (CORPAC), la temperatura alcanzó los 25.0 °C, con una anomalía de +7.6 °C por encima de los valores considerados normales. El registro del 30 de octubre marca un nuevo hito en las mediciones de temperatura nocturna de Piura durante este mes. El gráfico compartido muestra que, a lo largo de octubre, los valores presentaron variaciones, pero experimentaron un incremento durante los últimos días. Hasta el 20 de octubre, las temperaturas nocturnas se ubicaban principalmente entre los 22.5 °C y 24 °C. Sin embargo, desde el día 21 se observa una tendencia al alza, con registros que superaron los 24 °C y alcanzaron los 25.0 °C al cierre del mes. El reporte atribuye este récord al contexto del denominado El Niño Extraordinario, que se relaciona con las condiciones de temperaturas elevadas registradas en la región. La anomalía de +7.6 °C evidencia la magnitud de la diferencia respecto a los valores habituales para esta época del año. Este comportamiento también pone en atención las condiciones climáticas que enfrenta Piura, donde las altas temperaturas pueden mantenerse incluso durante las horas de la noche.

articles.title: Papa León XIV en el Cusco: Descartan instalar helipuerto en Sacsayhuamán para el ‘Papacóptero’
articles.summary: Este jueves 29 de octubre la comitiva del Vaticano, enviada al país a fin de inspeccionar los lugares por donde pasará el papa León XIV en su periplo peruano, llegó hasta el Cusco a fin de revisar los sitios que visitará el sumo pontífice.
articles.body_text: Este jueves 29 de octubre la comitiva del Vaticano, enviada al país a fin de inspeccionar los lugares por donde pasará el papa León XIV en su periplo peruano, llegó hasta el Cusco a fin de revisar los sitios que visitará el sumo pontífice. Según informó el diario ‘Correo’, la comitiva llegó al aeropuerto Alejandro Velasco de Cusco y posteriormente se trasladó hasta el Complejo Arqueológico de Sacsayhuamán por una ruta alterna, ya que maestros del Sutep realizaban una protesta en la plaza mayor. Una vez en el sitio, la comitiva, Cancillería, Arzobispado del Cusco, autoridades cusqueñas, Policía, Bomberos, Indeci, y otros, inspeccionaron la explanada principal, donde se instalará un escenario y seis pantallas gigantes para los asistentes al evento del 15 de noviembre. En el sitio, los bomberos, Seguridad del Estado y Policía, determinaron los sitios de acceso, salida y escape en caso de contingencia, avalados por la seguridad particular del Papa en el Vaticano y su cuerpo de resguardo. Se aprobó la disposición de ya no levantar un helipuerto en Sacsayhuamán para el ‘Papacóptero’, como se señaló en un principio. En caso de contingencia el sumo pontífice deberá ser trasladado en una ambulancia hasta el aeropuerto de Cusco, donde tendrá un helicóptero M17 a su disposición. Sobre las facilidades para el desplazamiento del ‘Papamóvil’ o vehículos de emergencia durante el recorrido del Papa, ningún vehículo circulará a través de la ruta que une el aeropuerto con el centro de la ciudad y Sacsayhuamán. De esta manera, las calles y avenidas permanecerán libres y sin tráfico en lo que dure la visita papal. En la Plaza Mayor de Cusco se tenía prevista la instalación de un gran escenario en el atrio de la Catedral, sin embargo, ahora esto habría quedado descartado, acordándose que el Papa se dirigirá a los suyos a ras de piso, aprovechando el desnivel a favor que tiene la basílica respecto a la plaza. Se supo que habrá cambios en la instalación de pantallas gigantes para los creyentes. En primera instancia se concibieron dos en el atrio y una tercera a la altura de la calle Santa Catalina Angosta, esta última sería levantada. En tanto, una cuarta pantalla está prevista a ser erigida en un espacio entre la calle Córdova del Tucumán y calle Suecia. Otras pantallas gigantes serán instaladas por pares en la plaza San Francisco y plaza Regocijo. El aforo para Sacsayhuamán se mantiene en un promedio de 80 mil visitantes divididos en seis sectores y en la plaza mayor unos 35 mil creyentes. Para ambos sitios las puertas se abrirán a las 06:00 horas y el acceso se dará únicamente a través de pases con códigos QR. “Se contratará un servicio de seguridad privado que va a ser el responsable por los ingresos. Todo será de acuerdo a los pases que se obtengan por Internet, aunque esto todavía no se sabe bien cómo se va a hacer”, señaló el monseñor Israel Condorhuamán, vicario de Cusco. Las autoridades estiman que 500 mil personas llegarán a Cusco por la visita del papa León XIV. Por ello, 4.000 policías custodiarán el orden y la seguridad del evento. Un contingente llegará procedente de Lima, Arequipa y Puno para apoyar a los efectivos locales. Se prevé que 3 horas en promedio estará el papa León XIV en la Ciudad Imperial, desde las 10:00 a.m. hasta las 1:00 p.m. el 15 de noviembre, tras lo cual partirá a Pucallpa.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

And now, Silicon Valley has entered the picture. Two-year old AI-first law firm Crosby has put in a bid to buy some of the assets of Weil Gotshal, including its trademark, its brand, and some unspecified internal data, TechCrunch has confirmed. Separately, it is also working to hire some of the firm’s 1,200 lawyers. The Information was first to report this offer. The once-prestigious Weil Gotshal confirmed to the New York Times this week that it was preparing to vote on dissolution in the coming days. The wind down is happening after the firm’s presumed leadership heir apparent turned down the role, a number of its top-producing lawyers left, and a hoped for merger with its rival, Willkie Farr & Gallagher, was shelved, the Times reported. Meanwhile, Crosby’s founders believe they are the future of law firms. Rather than selling their internally developed AI tech to existing firms like Harvey or Legora, Crosby is an actual law firm. It uses its AI to provide legal services at, the startup promises, a speed never before possible. The startup has raised about $85 million, including a $60 million Series B round in March led by Lux and Index, with participation from its seed-lead Sequoia, Elad Gil, 01 Advisors, and Bain Capital Ventures. Crosby came out of stealth mode in 2025 armed with $5.8 million in seed money. While no one has pointed to the rise of legal AI as a contributing factor to Weil Gotshal’s downfall, AI may be key to the legal industry’s future. Terms of the bid weren’t disclosed and there’s no guarantee that Crosby will prevail. But if it does, Weil Gotshal’s legacy could somehow rise from the ashes, transformed by an AI-first firm. articles.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Satlyt ran a successful test this month bringing it closer to turning spacecraft, starting with satellites, into virtual data centers.
articles.body_text: Naturally, Rama Afullo’s first reaction was, “Let’s GOOOO,” he said. His company, Satlyt , is building software to turn existing satellites into data processing networks, similar to the orbital data center concept. And he just took another step closer to that. After 13 months of work, the company had a successful test earlier this month. Working with the University of Houston on a NASA-funded research project, the test showed how the startup’s software can spread out tasks among computers while in orbit based on communication and available compute. He said the goal is to create software that connects to multiple satellites to share computing assignments. Users of the system “will only need to define permissions, priorities, and operating limits,” while the software will make decisions within those limits, Afullo told TechCrunch. Its software is already on three satellites in orbit and the first step to that vision was this test. While the test used NASA-funded research, the agency has not yet selected it for any particular mission or chosen it to deploy its technology. Afullo said NASA missions face the same constraints that Satlyt hopes to address — “limited computing resources, intermittent communication, and the need to get useful information back to people.” In this test, the company created a simulated network with four computers, four users, and eight services. The software then assessed how to assign and run tasks on those computers, accounting for compute and communication availability. One physical computer aboard a spacecraft ran the experiment, evaluating a simulated network of four computing hosts, then returned the results to Earth. The test proved that Satlyt’s software can generate plans on hardware in orbit, but more testing will be done to see how those computers transfer information amongst each other in practice when multiple physical computers are used. “The finding is a trade-off,” he said. One approach worked best, though it required more computing power than the others. Still, Satlyt which was in the top five of TechCrunch Disrupt Battlefield this year, calls this a win. “It’s a building block toward satellites sharing computing work,” he said. NASA already has a technology network designed to move data through space even when communication links face delays. It started using this tech earlier this year and has already tested it on aircraft. Afullo, who previously worked at Google and SpaceX, founded Satlyt in 2024 to turn spacecraft into virtual data centers. Its software helps operators run AI and other applications onboard, processing data closer to where it is collected and reducing dependence on downlinks, where satellites send data back to Earth, and ground-based analysis. For example, if a spacecraft sees a wildfire on Earth, such software can help it transmit relevant information much faster. “The goal is to get useful answers to people sooner and make better use of limited communication windows,” he said. “This experiment tested one planning component of that broader capability.” Satlyt said it still needs to test its own software under various workloads, hardware, and connectivity conditions. They also found an issue in how their software was time-referencing delays, Afullo said — it was stamping it as arrival time (the time it arrived) rather than elapsed delay (how long it took to arrive), which is a different metric. It doesn’t mean the experiment failed, however. “The software development, onboard execution, and return of outputs succeeded,” he said.

articles.title: Google's first data center satellite is online and writing poetry | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The first TPU in space is running a Google DeepMind Gemma 4 model and writing cheesy poetry.
articles.body_text: Google Suncatcher’s prototype space data center is online and communicating with the ground after launching earlier this month alongside more than 100 other spacecraft on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The satellite, which carries four Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and generates up to 1 kW of electricity, is intended to pave the way for future networks of close-flying satellites performing large inference workloads in orbit. However, the power demands of the TPU mean it can only turn one on for about 20 minutes at a time, complicating the already tricky business of space-to-ground communications. After a commissioning process that tested out the satellite’s subsystems over about three weeks, the spacecraft was ready to work. When engineers on the ground sent their first prompt this week, they asked the model pre-loaded onto the satellite, Google DeepMind’s Gemma 4, to write a haiku about being in space. And thus: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Google said it tested the model with these space-themed limericks (they should have sent a poet?) and, perhaps more importantly, the company asked the spacecraft to report on the orbital conditions around the satellite. A spokesperson told TechCrunch that the satellite was operating nominally. The ongoing test campaign will examine how the chips perform under thermal stress and in the space radiation environment. Google has extensively tested its TPUs in particle accelerators on Earth, but now needs to see how radiation’s real effects on their hardware in space affect their processor. Radiation can cause “bit flips” — causing a stored value in computer memory — and that in turn can corrupt data without triggering typical monitoring tools. Testing on the ground suggested the impact of radiation would be minimal for inference workloads and more of a problem for training a model, but now the Google team will get to assess those dynamics in reality, not a simulation. If the TPUs onboard this spacecraft prove capable, the next step will be launching two more satellites equipped with the advanced chips in 2027. Those spacecraft will support higher power generation and demonstrate inter-satellite optical links. Google’s Suncatcher project is largely alone among visions for space-based data centers in planning on high-speed links between the satellites to support coherent distributed workloads; SpaceX’s data centers are also expected to use laser links but also to orbit too far apart to share processing effectively. Companies like Starcloud and Cowboy Space expect to perform inference loads on individual satellites. Google and SpaceX’s visions are closely linked. Alphabet, Google’s parent company, holds a significant investment stake in SpaceX. And to launch their orbital data centers, both companies will require Starship, the still-in-development heavy-lift rocket at the center of Elon Musk’s space vision, to be fully and rapidly reusable. In a peer-reviewed analysis published earlier this month, Suncatcher researchers estimated that SpaceX would need to fly Starship 1,800 times to achieve the same learning-driven cost reductions it saw with its earlier vehicles. Suncatcher is a classic Google moonshot — the company’s focus is on designing infrastructure that will be economical in the 2030s. Getting there, however, may depend on how the rest of the company responds to the pressures and opportunities of AI in the near term. Alphabet, Google’s parent company, saw its stock plunge this week after reporting that efforts to insert AI into its search businesses are hurting ad revenue growth.

articles.title: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz warns that the AI boom is 'a great opportunity to go deceive people' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The cautionary Theranos tale takes on a new significance in the AI era, when companies that have never turned a profit are raising capital at trillion-dollar valuations.
articles.body_text: “ You Can See Everything ,” the documentary capturing disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes’ final weeks before prison, is sparking national conversation as it becomes one of the highest-grossing documentaries of all time. The film, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, intentionally refuses to characterize Holmes as a master manipulator or victim, instead highlighting her uncanny, almost hypnotic knack for making people pity her, even when they’re well aware of her crimes . Tyler Shultz didn’t need to see “You Can See Everything” to make up his mind about Holmes. Shultz, whose first job out of college was at Theranos, was a key whistleblower who exposed the company’s dangerously inaccurate blood testing devices, which made their way into Walgreens stores and delivered faulty results to real patients. (Theranos reached a peak valuation of around $10 billion despite its technology never actually working — the company only used its own machines for a fraction of tests , instead outsourcing others to third-party equipment.) There is little reason to keep talking about Holmes — her case is closed, and she’s in federal prison — but her con-artistry has fascinated the media ( myself included ) for the last decade. In fact, as Shultz says in an interview with The San Francisco Standard, “the only reason we’re talking about Elizabeth Holmes right now is because she wants us to be talking about Elizabeth Holmes right now.” But the cautionary tale of Theranos takes on a new significance as we enter the peak of the AI era, when companies that have never turned a profit are raising capital at trillion-dollar valuations. “I think the days of having a thirty-minute coffee with someone and sending them $100,000 should be over. Elizabeth took that model and scaled it to $100 million,” Shultz told SF Standard . His grandfather, former U.S. Secretary of State and Secretary of the Treasury George Shultz, was a notable investor and board member himself. “I believe that what [Holmes] did was raise the biggest angel round of funding of all time, but even at the smaller levels, I think investors need to recognize that when they put that type of money in someone’s hands, they are giving them tremendous power,” he added. Theranos’ funding often came from individual investors like the DeVos and Walton families, rather than venture firms. Theranos did not share scientific information or evidence that its machines worked with potential investors, citing concerns about revealing trade secrets, which warded off many top venture capitalists in Silicon Valley. At the time Theranos’ fraud was uncovered, it was seen as a shrill wake-up call for investors that they need to prioritize due diligence. But in the AI era, Shultz worries that investors may forget these lessons. “A huge danger with AI is that I think it is really hard to do due diligence on it,” he said. “It’s really hard to tell the difference between what is something truly unique and new versus like, a ChatGPT wrapper… If you want to deceive people, I think this is a great opportunity to go deceive people.” The first question posed by “You Can See Everything” lies in the premise of the movie itself. Why would a mother of two young children choose to invite a film crew to follow her final days with her family before surrendering to serve a prison sentence of over 11 years? The film poses questions that seem inscrutable, but this one seems pretty clear. She wants people to pity her, because this pity could be more useful for her future endeavors than hate or mockery.

articles.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hackers working for North Korea are suspected of hacking a Binance employee's laptop, which allowed the theft of billions in crypto.
articles.body_text: Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance . The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers. The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change. In a post on X , Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto. The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains. Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.” Spokesperson Andie Cooper said in a statement shared with TechCrunch on Friday that some $3 billion has been frozen by industry partners. The spokesperson said Binance has “begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.” It’s unclear how the hack went down or under what circumstances the employee’s laptop was compromised, but it’s not uncommon for security incidents to stem from the use of compromised software on employee devices. Software is generally built from many components, including open source projects, which hackers regularly target , compromise and modify in order to steal data from devices that the affected software is installed on. Other times, malware bundled with regular-looking apps and games can allow hackers to steal usernames, passwords, and session tokens from infected computers, which may let them log in as if they were a legitimate employee. Binance will face questions about why the company’s security allowed a single employee’s laptop to access systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in funds. Spokespeople for Binance did not respond to an email with questions about the breach. TechCrunch has also asked the company who, if anyone, performed a security audit of Binance’s network and systems prior to the hack. Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review. Security researchers at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and forensic company, attributed the breach to North Korean hackers, and called it the “largest hack in history.”

articles.title: DoorDash said it's only received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents | TechCrunch
articles.summary: DoorDash said that it is open to working with third-party agent makers.
articles.body_text: There’s a big uproar about AI agents taking over commerce and orders, but that might not be the case just yet. Delivery company DoorDash revealed during its third-quarter earnings call that it has only seen “several hundred” orders from third-party agents like Muse, Instinct, Fo, and others. For comparison, the company said in its 2025 report it completes an average of 3 million deliveries daily. “I would say that this [using agents to order] is something that is still a very dynamic area. And my take on all things technology is you never want to fight gravity. But at the same time, you don’t want to be delusional,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in an answer to an analyst’s questions about the topic. “What I mean by that is if you look at where AI agents are today, we’re seeing maybe several hundred orders in total from some of these third-party agents,” he said. Xu mentioned that users are still predominantly placing orders through DoorDash’s app. However, the company wants to learn more about agentic use cases and develop a healthy relationship with third-party agent makers. He added that, in the future, there could be an opportunity for it to advertise within these agents. DoorDash has its own agents, including a text-to-order agent it launched in September , a CLI agent introduced in July , and a chatbot called Ask DoorDash it launched in June, which allows users to place orders through prompts and photos . The company also released an MCP to enable ordering from other chatbots for corporate ordering. The space of agent-based ordering is evolving, as websites are still deciding whether to allow them to access their content or not. Amazon has been blocking such personal agents, but Walmart has laid out a red carpet for them in order to snag some business from its competitors . articles.title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Runware is building a factory to turn out prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line. The real test will be whether it can deliver at that scale.
articles.body_text: AI infrastructure company Runware is making news again, just months after unveiling the Sonic Inference Pod, a modular data center built in a factory and shipped to customers ready to install. Now the company has bigger plans. It told TechCrunch it wants to build a factory that assembles these pods on a production line, as if they were cars. The idea isn’t entirely new. Companies like Crusoe and Schneider Electric also sell prefabricated pods, but Runware says it can ship its pods faster. Flaviu Radulescu, co-founder and CEO of Runware, told TechCrunch that the company plans to scale production at its Romania-based factory to 30 megawatts of data center capacity per day by 2028, or nearly 1 gigawatt per month. That’s a whole lot of capacity: At that pace, Runware would produce roughly as much in a year as the entire U.S. was expected to add in data center power this year, about 10 gigawatts . But it also reflects an industrywide push to deploy data centers faster and more efficiently. Nvidia announced, for example, the Vera Rubin AI factories and the DSX POD earlier this year. Both are also meant to make it faster and easier for companies to build their own AI data centers. The difference with Runware, though, is that it says it has actually built a factory rather than just designed the infrastructure that would let others build one. Radulescu said Runware will gradually increase production starting next year and that it already has two factories — one it has used for a few years to build the pods, and a second it started building earlier this year. The second is expected to be finished within months and go online early next year. Runware will manufacture the modular data centers on an assembly line. Customers can provide their own site to assemble them, or Runware can find one for them. Radulescu said Runware aims to bring the pods online within 48 hours. That time covers installation and set-up time, not build time. A pod once took three weeks to build but it will soon take one day as it ramps up production, says the company. Runware will provide spare parts if components fail. Customers can also rent compute from Runware or supply their own GPUs and pay a monthly fee for the pods and operations. Power and internet are charged separately, he said. The pods can also be customized to customer preferences, he said. The pods have a standard design, but can be configured to meet customer requirements and the latest GPU chips. Chips can take a long time to arrive after they’re ordered, which works in Runware’s favor. “Our pod delivery times are also shorter than current GPU lead times, giving us time to adapt the infrastructure to the hardware being ordered,” he said. “For new GPU generations, our in-house hardware team can design, build, and test components itself, allowing us to adapt quickly.” Right now, these are all plans — execution is the test. The factory will need a lot of people, inventory, supply-chain logistics, and money. There are cautionary tales about reinventing manufacturing, notably the electric vehicle startup Arrival, once valued at over $13 billion , which struggled to mass-produce electric vehicles cost-effectively compared with traditional plants. Runware, which has raised more than $60 million to date, said it plans to raise a Series B, but for now it is finishing and launching the factory with the $50 million Series A it raised last December. “Our cost structure is very different,” Radulescu said, explaining how Runware seeks to avoid Arrival’s fate. “We do have headcount and materials cost,” he continued. “But our factory staff is cost-effective relative to the value of deploying compute for AI.” He also said that designing its own systems and buying widely available, affordable parts helps keep costs low. “We’ve brought in a highly experienced plant manager from the automotive industry to work alongside our chief of hardware and help us get that execution right.” Sourcing components could also be a challenge. Though Runware says it designs and builds its own cooling and other pod systems with standard components, some parts, such as pumps and fans, come from Germany, and it still depends on Nvidia for networking. Still, Runware claims it has received $1 billion in committed interest for its Sonic pods since it began offering them to outside customers a month ago, “representing over 20 megawatts, which we’re now working to deliver,” Radulescu said. Data centers in the U.S. and abroad have come under fire for how much energy they consume and how that affects the grid and other resources. When pressed, Radulescu said his company’s pods only need power and an internet connection. They’ll use a closed-loop liquid cooling system with air-cooled radiators to release heat, so they don’t really need a water connection. “We’re working with power providers on a site pipeline covering 397 megawatts, with potential to expand to 1.2 gigawatts,” he said, referring to its list of planned sites and adding that the company is deploying its modular data centers on sites that are much smaller than those used by hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. The sites, he continued, typically already have power, so they shouldn’t further strain the grid or disrupt the community. The pods also run “completely silent up to temperatures of 86 degrees Fahrenheit. We use energy from renewable sources whenever possible,” he continued. “We are actively working on expanding our network of energy providers and sites. We’re aiming to have renewables as our main energy source.”

articles.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the UK | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Waymo will begin testing self-driving versions of Toyota's electric bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker.
articles.body_text: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K. Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the bZ in the North American market.) The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits. The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation. For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio. But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles. Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues. “This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement. articles.title: Andy Jassy says Prime Video is on track to earn 'tens of billions of dollars' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The success of blockbuster hits like "Project Hail Mary" and "Verity" is only part of the story, Amazon's CEO says.
articles.body_text: It’s been four years since Amazon bought MGM for $8.5 billion . But coming off the blockbuster success of this year’s hit movie “Project Hail Mary,” Hollywood has become a lucrative business for the e-commerce giant. Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable , but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail. Amazon said its movie studio, Amazon MGM Studios, has brought in more than $1.2 billion in global box office sales so far this year, helped by hits like “Project Hail Mary” and “Verity.” “Project Hail Mary” grossed an estimated $684 million worldwide, according to The Numbers . Starring Ryan Gosling and based on Andy Weir’s novel , the film opened in theaters in March and became Amazon MGM Studios’ highest-grossing release, according to entertainment reports. (The studio also had at least one notable flop this year: “Melania.” ) Jassy also named a number of TV shows as hits, including “Carrie,” “The Summer I Turned Pretty,” “The Boys,” “Off Campus,” “Fallout,” and “Reacher.” Season 4 of “Reacher” drew 66 million viewers globally in its first 28 days, the company says, with more to come. Season 5 is filming now, and the show was picked up for a sixth season. (And if you don’t follow Alan Ritchson, the star of “Reacher,” on Threads, you are missing out on an actor who has turned a friendly-yet-witty reply into an art form.) Sports have also been a significant driver. Prime Video broadcasts NASCAR, the Masters, and UEFA Champions League soccer, but Thursday Night Football appears to be its biggest success this year. The first six games of this season have averaged 17.7 million viewers, up 16% from last year, according to Nielsen figures Amazon shared. articles.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian's best-selling vehicle | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Rivian is seeing strong enough sales of the new EV that it improved its guidance to Wall Street for the second time this year.
articles.body_text: Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV. While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000. It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate. The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian. “In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday. Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois. Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year. Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. Even cheaper versions are slated for 2027, which will be available for as low as $44,990. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Google’s new Jules AI agent will help developers fix buggy code
articles.summary: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that uses Gemini 2.0 to automatically fix Python and Javascript coding errors.
articles.body_text: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that can automatically fix coding errors for developers. Jules was introduced today alongside Gemini 2.0, and uses the updated Google AI model to create multi-step plans to address issues, modify multiple files, and prepare pull requests for Python and Javascript coding tasks in GitHub workflows. Microsoft introduced a similar experience for GitHub Copilot last year that can recognize and explain code, alongside recommending changes and fixing bugs. Jules will compete against Microsoft’s offering, and also against tools like Cursor and even Claude and ChatGPT’s coding abilities. Google’s launch of a coding-focused AI assistant is no surprise — CEO Sundar Pichai said in October that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is now generated by AI. “Jules handles bug fixes and other time-consuming tasks while you focus on what you actually want to build,” Google says in its blog post. “This effort is part of our long-term goal of building AI agents that are helpful in all domains, including coding.” Developers have full control to review and adjust the plans created by Jules, before choosing to merge the code it generates into their projects. The announcement doesn’t say that Jules will spot bugs for you, so presumably it needs to be directed to a list of issues that have already been identified to fix. Google also says that Jules is in early development and “may make mistakes,” but internal testing has shown it’s been beneficial for boosting developer productivity and providing real-time updates to help track and manage tasks. Jules is launching today for a “select group of trusted testers” according to Google, and will be released to other developers in early 2025. Updates about availability and how development is progressing will be available via the Google Labs website.

articles.title: Binance will buy FTX after liquidity crisis rumors
articles.summary: The world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance, has signed a nonbinding letter to acquire the third-largest exchange, FTX. The agreement comes after Twitter beef between the founders.
articles.body_text: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has signed a letter of intent to buy competitor FTX, the third-largest exchange by volume. The acquisition came after a CoinDesk article prompted speculation about FTX’s balance sheet. The terms of the deal weren’t disclosed. The letter of intent is nonbinding, and Binance CEO Changpeng “CZ” Zhao said the firm will conduct due diligence before the acquisition. Binance’s acquisition came after CZ said on Sunday he’d sell FTX’s FTT token, leading to a plunge in the token’s value. That token was the biggest asset on the balance sheet of Alameda Research, the trading firm also founded by Sam Bankman-Fried, the CEO of FTX, according to CoinDesk’s story. Bankman-Fried said yesterday that CZ’s Binance was attempting to target FTX “with false rumors.” Today, Bankman-Fried said that “rumors in media of conflict between our two exchanges” were exaggerated and that the Binance acquisition will help clear out a backlog of customer withdrawals. Earlier this year, Bankman-Fried rescued BlockFi and Voyager Digital, two troubled crypto lenders that were under threat of bank runs. He’s also cozied up to US lawmakers, donating more than $39 million in this election cycle — still less than he’d promised, which was $1 billion before 2024. By contrast, CZ’s Binance has been targeted by regulators in dozens of countries, including the US. The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Justice in the US are both probing Binance, according to The Wall Street Journal. The deal between the two companies isn’t totally done. “This is a highly dynamic situation, and we are assessing the situation in real time,” CZ said on Twitter. People pulled $1.4 billion from FTX on the Ethereum blockchain over the last day, according to The Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: Harley-Davidson spins out LiveWire as its own electric motorcycle brand
articles.summary: Harley-Davidson is spinning out its electric motorcycle division as a standalone company called LiveWire. A new electrified model will be unveiled in July.
articles.body_text: LiveWire, the first electric motorcycle from Harley-Davidson, will now become its own standalone brand. The Milwaukee-based company announced that it would be spinning out its electric motorcycle division as its own company with a distinct lineup and a tailored retail experience. Harley-Davidson plans to unveil the “first LiveWire branded motorcycle” on July 8th to coincide with the International Motorcycle Show. It’s a similar move to how Harley-Davidson approached its new electric bicycle company, Serial 1. The idea is that LiveWire continues to benefit from its relationship with its parent company while also forging its own brand identity that is distinct from Harley-Davidson. It’s a shift from how the company approached its current LiveWire model, in which the Harley-Davidson logo is front and center, while the LiveWire brand is practically nonexistent. And it’s a sign that going forward, Harley-Davidson is interested in letting its electrified models stand on their own terms. “With the mission to be the most desirable electric motorcycle brand in the world, LiveWire will pioneer the future of motorcycling, for the pursuit of urban adventure and beyond,” Jochen Zeitz, chairman, president, and CEO of Harley-Davidson, said in a statement. “LiveWire also plans to innovate and develop technology that will be applicable to Harley-Davidson electric motorcycles in the future.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22504479/3_LiveWire_Black_CMYK_PRIMARY_LOCKUP.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] There’s a new logo and a new “virtual” headquarters, with engineering teams stationed in Silicon Valley and Milwaukee. LiveWire will work with Harley-Davidson dealerships as an independent brand, with a blend of digital and physical retail formats. Asked whether this will include online ordering, a Harley-Davidson spokesperson responded with a cautiously worded statement. “It depends on the state in which you live,” the spokesperson said. “LiveWire is creating a purchase path that allows us to meet the expectations for a digital-first purchase experience, supported by a network of committed dealers that allow customers to choose their path and engagement model.” The question is whether this branding strategy will lead to better sales for Harley-Davidson’s electric models. Last year, Reuters reported that the company’s plan to appeal to a younger generation of motorcyclists with the LiveWire was struggling, with most of the preorders coming from older or preexisting customers. Harley-Davidson’s overall sales have been stagnant lately after hitting a low point in 2018. The problem could be that the price, which starts at $29,799, isn’t that much cheaper than a Tesla Model 3. Dealers told Reuters that many younger customers were turned off by the price tag. Harley-Davidson is also facing some stiff competition from rivals like Zero Motorcycles, which recently teamed up with power sports manufacturer Polaris on a new lineup of electric-powered ATVs and snowmobiles. And as the broader world of transportation shifts to electric, the company will be under increasing pressure from its shareholders to prove its vision for the future can be profitable.

articles.title: The Nvidia AI antitrust investigation is ‘escalating,’ reports Bloomberg
articles.summary: Nvidia and other companies have received subpoenas indicating a Department of Justice antitrust investigation into its AI chip business is moving forward.
articles.body_text: An antitrust investigation by the Department of Justice focusing on Nvidia’s AI dominance as the hardware company of choice is escalating, reports Bloomberg. The outlet reports that Nvidia and other companies have received legally binding requests for information as its sources say regulators are investigating whether Nvidia is “making it harder to switch to other suppliers and penalizes buyers that don’t exclusively use its artificial intelligence chips.” “Nvidia wins on merit, as reflected in our benchmark results and value to customers, and customers can choose whatever solution is best for them. We have inquired with the U.S. Department of Justice and have not been subpoenaed. Nonetheless, we are happy to answer any questions regulators may have about our business,” said Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo, as reported previously by CNBC. Earlier this summer, Nvidia had overtaken Microsoft as the world’s most valuable company, but now it trails both Microsoft and Apple. Before the subpoenas were reported on Tuesday afternoon, its share price dropped more than 9 percent, wiping out about $279 billion in market value in one day. But as Bloomberg notes, Nvidia’s stock is still up more than double this year as the AI boom has fueled sales of the company’s pricey chips, even after a report by The Information a few weeks ago saying that its upcoming Blackwell series of AI chips may be delayed “by three months or more due to design flaws.” Update, September 4th: Added Nvidia statement previously reported by CNBC.

articles.title: Uppgifter: Kris hos Riks – SD kan dra in miljonstöd
articles.summary: Flera medarbetare varslas och vissa har redan sagts upp, enligt uppgifter till SVT. Samtidigt kan Sverigedemokraterna vara på väg att dra in sitt miljonstöd, enligt Kvartals uppgifter.
articles.body_text: Det uppges krisa hos den SD-nära mediekanalen Riks. Flera medarbetare varslas och vissa har redan sagts upp, enligt uppgifter till SVT. Samtidigt kan Sverigedemokraterna vara på väg att dra in sitt miljonstöd, enligt Kvartals uppgifter. – Jag får faktiskt vara helt ärlig, jag har inte hört någonting, säger vd Jacob Hagnell. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Sedan starten av Riks 2020 har Sverigedemokraterna varit mediekanalens enskilt största finansiär. I dag kommer ungefär hälften av Riks intäkter från partiet – men framgent kan det bli noll kronor i stöd. En källa till Kvartal uppger att SD nu kan vara på väg att sluta helt med finansieringen. Jacob Hagnell, vd och chefredaktör för Riks har inte hört någonting från partiet om strypt bidrag till mediekanalen. – Jag har inte pratat med Sverigedemokraterna, om jag ska vara ärlig om det här. Och skulle det visa sig vara så att de inte vill fortsätta den här relationen, ja, då är det ju jättetråkigt. Men jag är ju väldigt tacksam för det stöd man har fått under åren. Han säger att han jobbat med att få upp lönsamhet och att kanalen i dag har andra inkomstkällor också. Uppgifterna om det minskade bidraget kommer samtidigt som en brinnande öppen debatt inom Sverigedemokraterna om synen på svenskhet. Riksprofilen Richard Sörman har varit en aktiv röst i den debatten där han och partiledningen stått på olika sidor. I en lång text hos Expressen har partiledare Jimmie Åkesson satt ner foten i frågan.

articles.title: Protest direkt mot Ryssland på toppmötet
articles.summary: Rysslands utrikesminister Sergej Lavrov har landat i Atlanta för helgens G20-möte. Men flera ministrar tog direkt ställning mot Ryssland – och vägrade gruppfoto.
articles.body_text: Rysslands utrikesminister Sergej Lavrov har landat i Atlanta för helgens G20-möte. Men flera ministrar tog direkt ställning mot Ryssland – och vägrade gruppfoto. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I helgen äger ett förberedande ministermöte för G20-ländernas utrikesministrar rum i Atlanta i USA, som ska pågå fram till och med lördag. På dagordningen står allt i från Ukraina till energipolitik. Ryssland är officiellt medlem av G20, men Putin har inte deltagit i möten på flera år. Det ryska utrikesdepartementet har redan meddelat att det tänker använda mötet för att argumentera mot sanktioner mot Ryssland – och den ryske utrikesministern Sergej Lavrovs närvaro har redan väckt känslor. Flera av hans internationella motsvarigheter vägrar nu att fotograferas tillsammans med honom. Till Dagbladet svarar den estniske utrikesministern Margus Tsahkna på frågan om han vill ta bild med Lavrov kort och gott: Två av de europeiska delegationerna har hittills vägrat, enligt Politico – medan övriga antingen inte svarat eller avböjt kommentar. En europeisk diplomat har dessutom uppgivit för sajten att man planerar två olika gruppbilder: En med Lavrov – och en utan. USA:s utrikesminister Marco Rubio ska ha ställt in fotograferingen efter att flera europeiska deltagare hotat att lämna den i protest mot den ryske utrikesministerns närvaro. G20 är en internationell samarbetsorganisation som består av världens 19 största ekonomier, samt Europeiska unionen och Afrikanska unionen. Under helgens möte väntas man diskutera konkurrensen mellan USA och Kina, kriget i Ukraina och spänningarna i Mellanöstern. EU:s utrikeschef Kaja Kallas, Frankrikes utrikesminister Jean-Noël Barrot och Tysklands utrikesminister Johann Wadephul är några av namnen på deltagarlistan. Årets toppmöte ska äga rum i Miami i december, då alla regeringschefer är inbjudna. Även Rysslands president, Vladimir Putin, har fått en inbjudan – men det är ännu oklart om han kommer dyka upp. Senast han deltog i ett möte var 2019. Samtidigt har Donald Trump ställt upp höga mål. Enligt The Atlantic vill presidenten att ett fredsavtal mellan Ryssland och Ukraina ska undertecknas i samband med toppmötet. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Paret döms till livstid efter dödsskjutningen
articles.summary: Isabell Eriksson, 34 och Joel Engback, 30, sköt ihjäl en gängmedlem. Nu döms de självutnämnda ”Bonnie and Clyde” till livstids fängelse.
articles.body_text: Isabell Eriksson, 34, skulle sitta i fängelse. I stället medverkade hon i ett mord mot en gängmedlem tillsammans med Joel Engback, 30. Nu döms de självutnämnda ”Bonnie and Clyde” till livstids fängelse. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den 24 oktober i fjol hördes skotten från Fornhöjden i östra Södertälje . En 18-årig gängmedlem hade dödats. Han befann sig i en bil tillsammans med två andra måltavlor – varav en skadades och en klarade sig oskadd. Skotten avlossades från en förbipasserande bil. Bakom ratten satt Isabell Eriksson, 34, medan Joel Engback, 30, öppnade eld. Enligt chattar som polisen tömt framgår det att gärningspersonerna hade en kärleksrelation vid tiden för brottet. De drömde om att lämna allt med pengarna från uppdraget , och kallade sig själva för ”Bonnie and Clyde”. Paret flydde brottsplatsen. Hemma hos Isabell Eriksson väntade hennes tvååriga dotter. Två dagar senare greps de och har nu dömts till livstids fängelse för mord, mordförsök och grovt vapenbrott. ”Mordet har närmast haft karaktären av ren avrättning och riktat sig mot en person utan möjlighet att värja sig” , står det i domen från Södertälje tingsrätt. Småbarnsmamman skulle inte ha befunnit sig i Södertälje vid tidpunkten för mordet. I april samma år hade hon dömts till fängelse för grovt narkotikabrott. Den 23 oktober skulle hon ha inställt sig hos Kriminalvården för att avtjäna ett treårigt fängelsestraff – men dök aldrig upp.

articles.title: Påven har röstat i amerikanska valet: ”Utövat sin rösträtt”
articles.summary: Påve Leo XIV är den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val. ”Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande.
articles.body_text: Påve Leo XIV är den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val. ” Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer ”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 3 november är det mellanårsval i USA. Nu har den katolska kyrkans ledare, påve Leo XIV, blivit den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val, skriver Chicago Sun Times. ” Påven Leo XIV har utövat sin rösträtt som amerikansk medborgare, närhelst han varit berättigad att göra det ”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande. Enligt Heliga stolens presskontor brukar påven använda sin rösträtt när han har rätt och möjlighet att göra det. Bland annat när han arbetade för den katolska kyrkan i Peru. ” Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer ”, skriver de i uttalandet. Påven har flera gånger kritiserat USA:s president Donald Trump för att bedriva en dålig utrikes- och migrationspolitik. Bland annat har han anklagat Trump för att ha ett storhetsvansinne. Det har fått den amerikanska presidenten att se rött. På Truth social har han tidigare anklagat påven för att vara ”usel” på utrikespolitik och svag på brottsbekämpning. – Jag är inte ett fan av påve Leo, har Trump sagt till reportrar. Utspelet kom efter ett inlägg på Truth Social om påven. ” Jag vill inte ha en påve som tycker det är okej för Iran att ha kärnvapen. Jag vill inte ha en påve som tycker det är hemskt att USA attackerade Venezuela. ”, skrev Trump i april.

articles.title: Svenske Mikael: ”Jag är skurken”
articles.summary: Kryssningsföretaget tiggde enorma summor pengar från sina passagerare – men i veckan blev det tvärstopp och 200 passagerare är strandsatta i Kambodja.
articles.body_text: Kryssningsföretaget tiggde enorma summor pengar från sina passagerare – men i veckan blev det tvärstopp och 200 passagerare är strandsatta i Kambodja. Svensken Mikael Petterson ligger bakom företaget. – Jag är skurken i den här historien, säger han till Business Insider . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Lyxfartyget ”The Odyssey” har den senaste tiden skapat rubriker över hela världen. Fartygets 203 passagerare är nu strandsatta i Kambodja efter ett halvår som har kantats av en stadigt sjunkande kvalitet ombord. – Jag är skurken i den här historien, men jag gör allt jag kan för att stötta de boende med en lösning, säger svensken Mikael Petterson, grundare av det ansvariga företaget Villa Vie Residences, till Business Insider. Samtidigt som internetuppkopplingen och maten rapporteras ha blivit sämre har kryssningsföretaget pressat de boende på pengar för att hålla sig självt flytande. Amerikanska pensionärsparet Lynn, 64, och Paul Montoya, 68, hade redan betalat 1,8 miljoner kronor för sin hytt, rapporterar Daily Mail. Nu har de pungat ut med totalt 4,4 miljoner kronor för vad som skulle bli en flerårig drömresa. Villa Vie Residences affärsidé var att hyra ut ”flytande hem” på fartyget ”The Odyssey”. Hytterna hyrdes ut i avtal som löpte över fem år eller längre men kunde också köpas som permanentbostäder.

articles.title: Paulina kan sova i ett dygn – är ändå alltid trött
articles.summary: Om Paulina Johansson Merkell, 34, sover i åtta timmar känns det som att hon inte har sovit på flera dagar. Så har det varit sedan hon fick den ovanliga sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni.
articles.body_text: Paulina Johansson Merkell, 34, kan ha sovit i åtta timmar – ändå känns det som att hon varit vaken i flera dygn. Hon lider av den ovanliga sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni. – Jag levde livet och sen bara ”pang” så var jag sängbunden nästan, säger hon. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter gymnasiet levde Paulina Johansson Merkell från Uppsala som en vanlig ung vuxen. Hon reste mycket, festade med vänner, skaffade ett heltidsjobb och hade planer på att börja studera. Men när hon inte orkade lika mycket som vännerna, somnade på jobbet och ständigt mådde dåligt förstod hon att någonting inte stod rätt till, vilket hon tidigare har berättat om för SVT Uppsala . Läkare tyckte hon var för ung för att vara så pass trött – och proverna visade ingenting avvikande – men efter många vårdrundor fick hon som 23-åring en diagnos: Den kroniska sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni. – Det var jättejobbigt. Alla ens kompisar och släkt levde vidare sina liv och jag var fast hemma och sov. Jag fick lägga om hela mitt liv och allting som jag hade tänkt för min framtid, säger hon. Idiopatisk hypersomni är en mycket ovanlig diagnos och innebär att man lider av extrem sömnighet på dagtid, trots att man sover normalt eller extra mycket, enligt Läkemedelsboken. Innan Paulina blev sjukskriven var arbetsdagarna plågsamma och till slut blev hon av med jobbet. – Jag ville inte aktivt ta mitt liv, men jag kände om det skulle hända någonting, om jag skulle dö, så skulle det inte göra någonting för då skulle jag slippa vara vaken. Som längst har hon sovit i 31 timmar i sträck, med undantag för korta vakna stunder för att äta något och gå på toa. En vanlig dag blir det 12-18 timmars sömn.

articles.title: Svensk forskare förbjuds resa in
articles.summary: Svenske forskaren och författaren Andreas Malm, 49, portas från att resa till Storbritannien.
articles.body_text: Svenske forskaren och författaren Andreas Malm, 49, portas från att resa till Storbritannien. – Jag blev ganska chockad, säger han till Expressen. Malm skulle medverka i ett arrangemang tillsammans med grundaren för den i landet terrorstämplade gruppen Palestine Action. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Andreas Malm, författare och humanekolog, har nekats inresa till Storbritannien, rapporterar The Guardian . Den brittiska immigrationsmyndigheten har nu nekat honom inresa eftersom hans närvaro ”kanske inte kan vara till gagn för allmänhetens bästa”. I onsdags fick Malm, docent vid institutionen för kulturgeografi och ekonomisk geografi vid Lunds universitet, ett mejl med beskedet. – Jag blev ganska chockad. Det borde jag kanske inte ha blivit. Men jag har åkt hur mycket som helst till Storbritannien i decennier, jag var där senast i maj och talade under en festival, säger Andreas Malm. Malm skulle under nästa vecka ha talat vid en konferens i London kallad ”Washingtons globala terrorvälde och Storbritanniens roll i att tvinga igenom det”. – Jag skulle tala om hur jakten på fossila bränslen är en del av de amerikanska krigen i Venezuela, Iran och övriga Mellanöstern, säger Malm. Malms tal skulle hållas tillsammans med Huda Ammori, en av medgrundarna till den i landet terrorstämplade organisationen Palestine Action. Storbritannien förbjöd Palestine Action i juli 2025 under landets terrorlagstiftning och det är även olagligt att uttrycka stöd för organisationen.

articles.title: Väljarna som sviker Trump: ”Ångrar mig”
articles.summary: De slöt upp bakom Trump i presidentvalet, till somligas förvåning. Men nu har många latinos i Texas fått nog. – Med tanke på allt som har hänt ångrar jag att jag röstade på honom, säger predikanten Cassandra Sarmiento.
articles.body_text: De slöt upp bakom Trump i presidentvalet, till somligas förvåning. Men nu har många latinos i Texas fått nog. – Med tanke på allt som har hänt ångrar jag att jag röstade på honom, säger predikanten Cassandra Sarmiento. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. De är tejanos, för att vara exakt. Ordet är spanskans motsvarighet till engelskans Texans (alltså ett uttryck för personer från Texas), men det spanska ordet syftar på de Texasbor som har mexikanskt ursprung. Tejano är också en en musikstil som hör hemma här vid gränsen mellan Mexiko och Texas. Den har mexikanska gitarrer men också stompiga dragspel, som kommer från tyskarna och tjeckerna som hamnade i Texas i drivor och tog med sig sin polka. Bobby Pulido har varit en av genrens stora stjärnor sedan 90-talet, när han slog igenom med ”Desvelado”, en smäktande ballad om en man som inte kan sova för han är så förälskad i en kvinna. Han har aldrig träffat henne, bara fastnat för hennes röst på radion. Nu är det andra röster som Pulido jagar. Han har nämligen sadlat om från tejanostjärna till demokratisk kandidat till representanthuset i Texas 15:e distrikt. Så det är kanske inte för mycket att gissa att han inte får så mycket sömn nu heller, de här sista nätterna inför valet. Det femtonde distriktet går som ett vingligt Jengatorn genom södra Texas, med start öster om San Antonio, och ner hela vägen till gränsen mot Mexiko. Här ner mot Rio Grande-dalgången gick Donald Trump från klarhet till klarhet i de senaste presidentvalen. 2016 förlorade han klart mot Clinton, 2020 vann han snävt mot Biden och för två år sen var det en kross med 17 procentenheter över Kamala Harris. Men efter snart en halv mandatperiod knakar det betänkligt i relationen mellan Trump och väljarna här. Pulido leder mot republikanen Monica de la Cruz, enligt mätningarna, trots att republikanerna har ritat om distriktskartan för att gynna sina kandidater. På ett nöjesfält i McAllen, en av gränsstäderna i distriktet, går folk omkring i neonljuset, käkar popcorn och håller ordning på uppspelta barn som springer ut från karusellerna.
